## Summary

Upgraded the toolchain to TypeScript 7.0.2 (the native Go compiler port) and proved it changes nothing shipped. Sequence: took a baseline on 6.0.3 first (vitest 1718 passed, 4 skipped, 100 files, 1 skipped file; full build; sha256 of all 26 dist files), then bumped the root devDependency to caret 7.0.2, reinstalled, and re-ran everything. Results: typecheck clean on both workspaces and 1.92s down to 0.52s, a 3.7x speedup; tests byte-identical to baseline at 1718 passed and 4 skipped; build declaration emit produced 23 of 26 dist files unchanged, including every shipped JS bundle. The three differing files are d.ts only and the diff is purely quote style, since TS 7 preserves the source quote style in emitted string-literal types where TS 6 normalised to double quotes; the types are identical and no consumer can observe it. npm also pulls a platform-specific native binary, here node_modules/@typescript/typescript-darwin-arm64. One behavioural difference worth remembering, recorded in the decision: TS 7 enforces consistent file-name casing against the invocation path where TS 6 normalised it, so invoking tsc through a differently-cased path than the repo canonical one raises TS1149; on this machine the shell starts in a lowercase io path while the repo is IO. Running the npm script is unaffected. dist is gitignored so no build output is committed. Initiative created without binding the branch, so main stays on session-driver for the peer session working 1.3.
